en: The Sūtra on the Secret Characteristics Spoken by the Buddha,

Volume One. Translated by the Tripitaka Master Śīlagupta, Dharma Master of the Transmission of the Dharma, Imperial Preceptor of the Court for the Promotion of Merit and Acting Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments,
recipient of the purple robe, and other monks, during the Western Heaven (India).
Translated by Imperial Decree. Thus have I heard:
At one time, the World-Honored One dwelt within the samādhi-realm of all Tathāgatas, surrounded by a complete assembly of all Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas.
At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, arose from the samādhi of the wisdom of all Buddhas and surveyed the entire great assembly.

While he was thus observing the congregation, all the Tathāgatas together with the multitude of Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas took their places, relying upon the lunar maṇḍala to the left of the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, standing before the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, joined his palms with sincere devotion and addressed him thus:
"World-Honored One!
"The secret ritual procedures are extremely profound and vast; how, then, should one practice them here in a concise manner?
Within these essential and abbreviated methods, I shall receive and practice them.
At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, praised the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, saying:
“Excellent, excellent, Vajrapāṇi!
You have now well inquired concerning the secret ritual procedures that are profound and vast; I shall now explain them to you in brief.”
This means that when a practitioner of yoga enters a house, they should first visualize secret syllables to perform the rite of protection and purification.
Specifically, one should visualize the syllable *A* at the tip of the tongue; this syllable is visualized as becoming a pure and wondrous moon disc (*candramaṇḍala*).
Upon that moon disc, one visualizes the syllable *Hūṃ*, which further becomes a five-pronged, white, great vajra (*mahāvajra*).
Having visualized in this manner, the practitioner should form the vajra-añjali mudrā and place it upon the crown of his head, reciting this great vidyā-mantra to perform the purification:
The Great Vidyā-mantra: Oṃ svabhāva-śuddhāḥ sarva-dharmāḥ svabhāva-śuddho ’haṃ. Having recited this great vidyā-mantra, the practitioner should next make this vow:

"I pray that all Buddhas of the ten directions and all Bodhisattvas will take me into their compassionate care. I, [Name], while performing this rite of accomplishment, shall from this day forth generate the unsurpassed mind of great bodhicitta, remaining firm and non-regressing until I sit upon the terrace of enlightenment."
Furthermore, he spoke in verse:
"May I be equal to the Buddhas of the three times, And certainly attain the state of a Most Honored Perfectly Awakened One!
May I be fully endowed with the precepts that gather wholesome dharmas, The precepts that gather moral discipline, And the precepts that benefit sentient beings."
May I uphold these three clusters of pure and sublime precepts with complete firmness.
May the Buddhas, the sublime Dharma, and the Saṅgha—the most supreme Triple Gem—bestow their protection;
may the original Triple Gem embrace me, and may I arise in accordance with all the Buddhas.
The vajra and its seal-bell, which I uphold, are all truly real.
May that Ācārya accept me; in the vast and supreme Vajra Family, I shall constantly practice the four kinds of giving, performing them thus at the six periods every day.
Through the practice corresponding to that Great Jewel Family, arising within samādhi with a superior aspiration,
I shall uphold all gateways of the true Dharma— those of the outer and inner vehicles, as well as those of the Three Vehicles.
Pure within the Great Lotus Family, you give birth to unsurpassed, supreme enlightenment;
in accordance with all vows, may you embrace me within the true Dharma.
Perform the rites of offering as appropriate; this is the most supreme among the Mahā-karmakula.

Generate the unsurpassed bodhicitta and all the sublime practices that arise from it, universally encompassing all conduct in its entirety, for the sake of bringing vast benefit and happiness to all sentient beings.
Those who have not yet crossed over, I shall cause to cross;
those who are not yet liberated, I shall lead to liberation.
For all those who have not yet attained peace, I shall open for them the gate of peace.
"May all sentient beings without exception universally abide in the ground of nirvāṇa.

At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, further proclaimed for the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi the fundamental dharma-gate of the true arising of all samādhis from the Samādhi of Universal Exhaustion:
"The practitioner should bind the seal of meditative concentration (dhyāna-mudrā)."

Having established oneself in accordance with the Dharma, one should contemplate that all phenomena are equal in their selflessness (*anātman*). If one perceives phenomena as having internal or external aspects, this constitutes an obscuration within the mind; one should know that apart from the mind, there are no separate phenomena.
Furthermore, one should reflect within the mind:
"All phenomena are unarisen and luminous by nature; this is the primordial non-arising nature of all phenomena."

Abiding in that state of mind according to one's contemplation, one should then recite the mantra syllables for awakening the fundamental mind with a voice that is naturally luminous and pleasing; while reciting and contemplating them, one should visualize the form of the moon-maṇḍala of the mind.
The *Mahāvyutpatti* states: "Oṃ citta-prativedha-vidhūnaya. Furthermore, the verse says:
"Perfectly true and utterly pure, it is like space, free from defilement and obscuration."
All coarse and heavy afflictions are entirely eliminated, and false conceptualizations are further shattered and dispelled.
Because those stains of affliction have been purified, he appears like the bright moon at its first rise;
the boundless mass of the Buddhas' merits all enters into the wondrous sign of the letter A.
"What are its characteristics?
They are as follows:

*ā ā ī e o ṛ ḷ i ai u au aṃ aḥ*. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi again took his stand within the Moon Maṇḍala of the Bodhicitta of the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, and addressed him thus:"
“World-Honored One!
What are the most supreme merits of the Moon Maṇḍala of the Bodhicitta?
At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, briefly explained the characteristics of the Moon Maṇḍala of the Bodhicitta for the sake of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi:
“Vajrapāṇi! You should know that when the infinite merits of all Buddhas enter such sublime signs as the letter ‘A,’ they possess a pure, radiant light like that of a crystal moon.”

Having entered, one further gives rise to the transformative activities of enlightened action from the mind of wisdom, which is luminously pure by its very nature; that is, one recites the subtle syllables of the Great Mantra and generates the bodhicitta.
The Great Illumination says:
“Oṃ jvati-cchinda mudrā-nayami. Furthermore, the verse states:
“Following this, the mind of great compassion arises, universally encompassing all the activities of sentient beings.”
All wholesome dharmas are perfectly complete, And one is entirely unattached to any afflictions.
Within the center and to the left and right of the moon-maṇḍala, The moon of bodhicitta is the second;
Into all the gateways of the Buddhas’ merit, One further enters the wondrous forms of the syllable KA and the rest.
"Having thus entered, one then becomes associated with the images of all phenomena.
What are their characteristics?
They are as follows:"

“Ka Kha Ga Gha Ṅa (nasal, pronounced lightly); Ca Cha Ja Jha Ña (pronounced with the *ren* and *zo* cuts); Ṭa Ṭha Ḍa Ḍha Ṇa (Ṇa pronounced level-toned and lightly); Ta Tha Da Dha Na (Na pronounced lightly); Pa Pha Ba Bha Ma (Ma pronounced lightly); Ya Ra La Va Śa Ṣa Sa Ha Kṣa. These syllables are the form of the Moon Maṇḍala of Bodhicitta.”
"The sequence of ritual applications and practices for this maṇḍala is as explained in other teachings.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi again took his place, relying upon the moon maṇḍala to the right of the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, and addressed him thus:
"Blessed One!"
"And how should one enter this right-hand Moon Maṇḍala?
At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, saying: "Vajrapāṇi!"
One should know that the vajra is itself vajra-wisdom, capable of generating the supreme mass of merit of all Buddhas.

As for the vajra, its form consists of five prongs, accomplished according to the ritual precepts; it is further surrounded by blazing flames. These rays of light issue forth from the heart of Samantabhadra, arising as the marks of various practices through the cause of firmness.
If one enters the maṇḍala, one should visualize one’s own body as the form of the five-wisdom vajra.
While performing this visualization, recite this great mantra: “Oṃ tiṣṭha vajra. Furthermore, a verse says:
“The Buddha, throughout three asaṃkhyeya kalpas, Cultivated and perfected the supreme conduct of Bodhi;”
From traversing the stages up to ascending to the rank of the Honored One of Wondrous Enlightenment—
all is due to pure, untainted wisdom.
The maṇḍala of the wondrous moon of bodhi is most supremely pure and free from all defilements.
"Within that, one should visualize the Wisdom-Vajra;
this is the five-wisdom vajra.

Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana. This signifies that the Vajradhara should further visualize the entire realm of empty space as being completely filled and gathered together to form the measure of a single great vajra. Thereafter, the practitioner should visualize his own body as the vajra, in accordance with the extensive or concise [ritual procedures].
While performing the visualization, recite this great mantra:
"Oṃ vajratmakūṃ. Furthermore, the verse says:
"The bodies of all Buddhas are entirely without obstruction and have no support;
Unborn, uncreated, pure, and flawless, within it even the nature of equality is transcended;
uninterrupted, unbroken, and indestructible, the Dharma-body is untainted and primordially pure;
born from a vajra-like solid essence, the Tathāgata’s vajra-body is unsurpassed.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, having taken his place within the lunar maṇḍala to the right of the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, addressed him thus:
"World-Honored One!..."
"Furthermore, how does one contemplate that vajra?
At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, having universally surveyed all the Tathāgatas, spoke these words:
"Listen attentively."
O Tathāgatas!
I shall now proclaim the characteristics of the visualization within the image of the Buddha.
What are those characteristics?
This is what is called the mark of the *sattva-vajra*.
One should contemplate that all those marks are fully complete; they are the very image of the Buddha.
While performing this visualization, recite this great mantra (*mahāvidyā*):
“Oṃ yathā sarvatathāgata-sthatasva. Furthermore, the verse says:
“The secret body of all Buddhas, And likewise their spheres, nature, wisdom, and conduct;
The Honored One who attains perfect awakening through the five signs— All these are fulfilled and utterly pure by the Buddhas.”
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi again took his place within the moon-maṇḍala behind the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, and addressed him thus:
"World-Honored One!..."
"What is this secret?
Furthermore, what are its sphere, nature, wisdom, and conduct?
At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, praised the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi and spoke these verses:
“Excellent, O Great Vajrasattva!
Excellent, O Vajra Holy Sublime Jewel;
excellent, O Vajra Gate of the True Dharma; excellent, O Vajra Multitude of Activities!”
This scripture well explains the secret meaning; it is the unsurpassed Vajrayāna.
All the secret gateways of the Buddhas and the Mahāyāna dharmas of direct realization are herein subsumed.
When practicing for accomplishment, there is sublime purity; having attained the fruit of Buddhahood, one gains wondrous bliss.
As for your question regarding what constitutes the "Secret" and so forth:
it refers to the lotus and the vajra.
This is the Great Secret of the Tathāgatas, from which all Buddhas are born.
"If one can contemplate according to the Dharma with a mind of truth, one shall attain Buddhahood in a single kṣaṇa.
*The Sūtra on the Secret Signs Spoken by the Buddha*, Fascicle Upper.
*The Sūtra on the Secret Signs Spoken by the Buddha*, Fascicle Middle.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Śīlagupta, Dharma Master and Imperially Conferred Rank of Chao Feng Da Fu,
Acting Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and Monk Subject Śīlagupta et al., by Imperial Decree. At that time,
the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi again addressed the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, saying:
“World-Honored One!
What is this vajra? And what is this lotus?”
At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, saying: "Vajrapāṇi!
The wisdom in which all Tathāgatas abide is the vajra; the harmonious union of the noble ones of one's own family is called the lotus."
And that vajra rests upon a lotus; from this, all Tathāgatas are born, and the bodies of those Tathāgatas are Vairocana!
Having performed this, one then arranges the secret syllables of the great mantra (*mahāvidyā*) according to the Vajra Speech.
That is to say: *bhrūṃ*.
Having first visualized this syllable as abiding within the pure moon-maṇḍala of one’s own heart, one then visualizes it becoming the Great Mount Sumeru.

Visualize these syllables appearing upon that mountain; those syllables further transform into a vast and lofty pavilion with a vajra-jewel peak, adorned with great maṇi jewels, suspended bells, precious gems, silk banners, and necklaces, which emit harmonious and elegant sounds as they are stirred by a gentle breeze.
Adorned with such various exquisite ornaments, auspicious, supreme, and worthy of praise, that pavilion is the common abode of all Tathāgatas;
within the pavilion, one should further visualize a five-pronged vajra-wheel, corresponding in its extent to the concise or detailed [ritual].

One should then visualize that the vajra transforms once more into the form of the Great Being Vajrasattva, endowed with all supreme marks, his body appearing like the color of the moon and radiating light.

He is seated upon a lunar disc, wearing a magnificent jeweled crown of the five Buddhas, adorned with a garland of blazing vajra-light flames. Both his left and right hands are raised in the gesture of elevation, as he dwells within the true principle of the great samādhi of the original lack of intrinsic nature of all phenomena.
Whether as the subjective mind or the objective vessel, all natures and self-natures are unified into a single characteristic; therefore, visualize yourself as the perfected Vajrasattva!
"Having observed in this manner, one should then perform the ritual applications of these deities and all other dharmas.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi again took his place within the moon maṇḍala before the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, and addressed him thus:
"World-Honored One!"
"What is this tutelary deity?
At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, sequentially expounded the teachings on the tutelary deities and other matters for the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi:

"All practitioners of yoga should first, according to the ritual, visualize the syllable 'HŪṂ' within the moon-maṇḍala of their own hearts. From this written character, they should bring forth the great vajra of manifold forms, which is the skillful activity of the Universal Gate."

When performing this visualization, one should form the *guhyamudrā* (secret seal). First, perform the *vajrabandha* (vajra-binding), then spread the fingers apart and make a gesture of drawing them inward to form the seal.

Recite this *hṛdaya-mantra* (essential heart mantra): *vajra bandha trāṭ*. Having recited this mantra and formed this seal, one may then form all other seals and perform the rites of the *iṣṭadevatā* (chosen deity) and so forth, including the *vajrāveśa* (vajra-possession), summoning (*ākarṣaṇa*), and other various methods of accomplishment. Through the empowering activity of the *vajras* of one’s own body, speech, and mind, one immediately attains the accomplishment of *vaśīkaraṇa* (subjugation/loving-kindness).
Thereupon, one should bind the Vajrāveśa mudrā and recite its heart-mantra.
That mantra is: *Āḥ*.

By means of this heart-mantra, all dharmas, including the deities and even other methods for accomplishment, are universally drawn in; they all become well-disposed, affectionate, and remain [in service].
As for the Vajrāveśa mudrā:
first form the vajra-palms, next form the vajra-bind, and finally bind the Vajrāveśa mudrā.
Regarding the *vajrapāṇi* (Vajra-Palm):

with the palms made firm and solid, the fingers are not bound but are held tightly together to form the *vajrapāṇi*. Then, by skillfully binding these palms, one forms the *vajrabandha* (Vajra-Bond). Next, opening this bond, one forms two *vajramuṣṭi* (Vajra-Fists) with the heads [of the thumbs] placed side-by-side; this constitutes the *vajrāveśa-samaya-mudrā* (Vajra-Entrance Samaya Seal).

Then, from within one’s own heart, one should visualize the form of the syllable of Vajrasattva; furthermore, one should visualize that syllable transforming into a great five-pronged white vajra, pure and exquisite, with radiant flames encircling it on all sides.
Furthermore, as before, one should visualize the secret syllables according to the ritual;
thereafter, one binds the Sattvavajra mudrā.
When binding this mudrā, one should first recite this heart mahāvidyā: "Oṃ samayasattva. As for the Sattvavajra mudrā:

This means: form the shape of a full moon with both hands; the two middle fingers are separated from each other while the remaining fingers touch their counterparts, forming a seal (*mudrā*) like the shape of a vajra.
When binding this seal, recite this great mantra (*mahāvidyā*): "Oṃ..."
Tiṣṭha vajra dṛḍha!
Mīṃ vaḥ (1) | Suduśayumīṃ vaḥ (2) |
Anurakto me bhava śāstuḥ.
Mīṃ va va | Su pu sa yo mīṃ va va || 4-5 ||
Hrīṃ dhyāmīti tiṣṭha sarva-
Siddhyanti pratyakṣa.
Sarvakarmāṇuśaya (Sarva-kar-mi-aṇu-śa-ya) 8.
Ejitaśriye (Ejita-śrī-ye)
KRU HŪṂ HA (9)
Hā hā hā hūḥ (ten times). "Such is the Great Illumination, which is the Dharma of the Honored One; within it are contained the four mudrās of reverential salutation."
That is to say:
the heart-seal;
the heart-seal of the vow and admonition;
The heart-seal of the Mahāyāna Abhimukha-samādhi;
the heart-seals of the five supernormal powers, such as the wondrous Vajra-wisdom and the divine eye-wisdom.
These various seals collectively encompass the firm nature of the Tathāgata; through the empowerment of the Vajra, one is freed from all fears and can accomplish all supreme siddhis.

All forms of satisfaction, bliss, and meditative absorptions (*samāpatti*), all gateways of dhāraṇī, and even the true nature (*tathatā*) of all Tathāgatas—having gathered these entirely within one’s own mind—one fully attains abiding in the vajra-empowered body, speech, and mental activities.
Thereafter, take silk cloth to fashion a garland and place it upon the crown of one's head, reciting this heart-mantra:
"Praṭīccha vajra hūṃ. Having empowered [the disciple] by reciting this heart-mantra, form the gesture of binding the garland upon the crown of the head and turn it to cover the face.
When binding the garland, in accordance with the ritual protocol, the Ācārya shall speak as follows:

"You now receive this secret heart-mantra (*hṛdaya-mantra*). This is the Dharma of the originally non-substantial nature of the World-Honored One of Valiant Great Power. Having obtained the true empowerment (*adhiṣṭhāna*) of the Ācārya, you shall be able to skillfully accomplish all activities. This was spoken by the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, and is likewise embraced by all Buddhas and Vajradharas."
Having spoken these words, he removed the silk cloth and recited this great vidyā-mantra:
“Oṃ vajrasattva svāhā | nīrya cūḍākṛtana tathu para uḍākṛtya sarvacū vajracū rānudraṃ he vajrapaśya. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi...
Furthermore, having taken his place within the lunar maṇḍala to the right of the Bhagavān Mahāvairocana Tathāgata, he spoke these verses in praise:
"How wonderful! O Honored One among all Perfectly Enlightened Ones!"
"The wisdom of samādhi is unsurpassed;
all sentient beings whatsoever attain Buddhahood through these two dharmas.
After the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi had offered this praise, he again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
What is the mode of appearance for the initial opening of the eyes?
At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, saying:
"Vajrapāṇi! 'Opening the eyes for the first time' means to gaze sequentially upon one's own great maṇḍala.

While gazing upon this maṇḍala, one immediately attains the empowerment of the majestic power of all Tathāgatas; one dwells within the heart of Vajrasattva in accordance with reality, and likewise beholds the supreme maṇḍala of various radiances."
Furthermore, they behold vast displays of supernatural powers and transformations.
By virtue of being sustained by the Tathāgata’s empowerment, they are able to see the body of Vajrapāṇi, or even behold the bodies of all the Tathāgatas.

At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Acala from within the assembly approached the World-Honored One, the Fundamental Natureless Tathāgata Mahāvairocana; having circumambulated him to the right, he addressed him thus:
"World-Honored One!
"What is this great maṇḍala?
How should I practice within it?
At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Acala, saying:
"The great maṇḍala refers to visualizing one’s own body as the maṇḍala.
Having visualized it thus, one takes the vajra-consecrated pure perfumed water for empowerment and recites this heart-mantra:
*vajravisphoṭa*. Then, having bound the garland-seal (*mālāmudrā*), one places the crown of all Buddhas upon the crown of one’s own head."
Regarding the Garland-Tying Mudrā:
first, interlace the two thumbs within the palms; then, bend the middle fingers so that their tips meet the surfaces of the thumbs to form the mudrā.
This is the mudrā of the Tathāgata family; the mudrās of the other four families are likewise used in the same manner.
The vidyās of the five families follow this sequence.
The vidyā is as follows:
Oṃ vajradhātviśvari hūṃ.
Vajriṇī (one phrase): "Oṃ vajravajriṇi"
HŪṂ (one syllable) OṂ RATNAVĀRĪNI (two syllables)
HŪṂ (one syllable) OṂ PADMA VAJRĪṆI (two syllables)
HŪṂ (one syllable) OṂ KARMABAJRIṆĪ (two syllables)

HŪṂ (one syllable). Having performed the consecration as previously described, without altering the previous mudrā, rotate the two index fingers twice to form the gesture of encircling; this constitutes the four mudrās for binding the garland.
Bind garlands at four locations—the crown of the head, the forehead, the throat, and behind the crown;

then proceed to both ears, rotate back from behind the crown to the front, and slowly descend while releasing the seal, performing this with firm adherence to the ritual procedures of the *Saṃgīti* teachings.
Furthermore, it is stated in the *Saṃpuṭa Tantra*:
"Next, the ācārya, having taken hold of the vajra and established himself according to the ritual, shall then address the disciple with these words of oath and admonition:
'Now you have received this from all the Buddhas and Tathāgatas!'"
Within this supreme secret dharma, having conferred the vajra empowerment,
I bestow upon you the vajra; may you skillfully accomplish all siddhis,
for the sake of those Tathāgatas!
By this, one attains Buddhahood.
Furthermore, he bestowed the Great Mantra, saying:

“Oṃ vajratīpatitva ma viśva-mi tiṣṭha vajra-samayas tvaṃ. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, having again taken his place within the lunar maṇḍala to the right of the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, addressed him thus:
“World-Honored One!
What is this ‘self-vajra’?
At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, saying:

“Vajrapāṇi! As for the vajra itself, it is the Tathāgata’s vajra: twelve finger-widths in length, five-pronged, fashioned with an excellent and beautiful appearance, devoid of blazing flames, and composed of gold or similar materials.”
As for that vajra of Vajrasattva, it is fashioned with five prongs of indefinite proportions; it possesses fierce and blazing flames and is composed of various jewels such as padmarāga.

The Vajra Kings and other great Vajradharas, as well as the Vajrakrodhas and Vajrayakṣas—such vajras as these are all twelve finger-breadths in length, three parts in height, five-pronged, and fashioned with sharp points.
The characteristics of these vajras are explained in detail in the *Mahāyānābhisamayakrama-tantra* and the *Trailokyavijaya-tantra*; here they are indicated only briefly.
Once the yoga practitioner has recognized the characteristics of the vajra, they are thereafter called one who has received the great vajra empowerment.
Furthermore, the mantra is as follows:

Oṃ vajrasattva-ma-viśodhaya | vajranātha-mo-piśyaka-ta | he vajranātha-ma-sa | yai-yai-ta-nama | tathāgata-ye-mi || Having received the empowerment, one may then receive the great vajra of the accomplishments of all Buddhas.
Furthermore, the verse says:
“You shall always hold this vajra; it is the firm vow of Vajrapāṇi.
In the supreme cultivation of Vajrasattva, all attain Buddhahood through this.”
Furthermore, the great vidyā-mantra is as follows:

“Oṃ sarvatathāgata-siddhi-vajra-samaye tiṣṭha īśvaradhāraṇīye vajrasattva hī hī hī hī hūṃ. Thereafter, from the samādhi of the Great Seal (mahāmudrā) of the mind of Samantabhadra, he spoke this heart-vidyā-mantra accordingly:

“*Mahā-samaya-sattva-samayas-tvaṃ* (1) *mahā-samaya-sattvā-haṃ* (2) *mahā-samaya-sattva-atiṣṭha svāhā* (3). By means of this seal and mantra, Vajradhara and all the other bodhisattvas are entirely and equally accomplished within that Great Samaya of the Reality of All Seals.
Furthermore, the heart-mantra (hṛdaya-mantra) formed from the vajras of body,

At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi again addressed the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, regarding the originally non-substantial nature of phenomena, inquiring with the wisdom of investigation:
“World-Honored One!...”
"How should the supreme samādhi be cultivated?
At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, praised the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi!
He then spoke in verse:
“Excellent, O Great Vajrasattva!
Excellent, O Vajra of Wondrous Jewels!”
Excellent is the Vajra Dharma-gate; excellent is the supreme Vajra activity!
To skillfully explain the secret meaning of this sūtra is itself the unsurpassed Vajrayāna;
within the secrets of all Tathāgatas, it encompasses all the Mahāyāna dharmas of direct realization.
The Buddha said:
“Vajrapāṇi! One who wishes to cultivate samādhi should first cause [the deity] to abide before them by means of the Vajrāṅkuśa mudrā and the hook of the great mantra.”
Next, one should perform the invitation using the Vajrapāśa mudrā and its great mantra;
then, one should cause [the deity] to remain firmly established using the Vajrasphoṭa mudrā and its great mantra;
finally, one should perform the awakening and the āveśa (possession) using the Vajraghaṇṭā mudrā and its great mantra.
The respective great vidyās are as follows:

“VAJRĀṄKUŚA JAḤ (1); VAJRAPĀŚA HŪṂ (2); VAJRASPHOTA BAṂ (3); VAJRAGHAṆṬĀ ĀḤ (4). Thereafter, having bound the samaya-mudrā of the respective deity, one should contemplate the respective seed-syllables with a concentrated mind.
That is to say:
"JṚṂ HŪṂ VAṂ HOḤ. This is the method for cultivating samādhi.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi again stood before the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, and spoke these verses:
"How wonderful! All Honored Ones of Perfect Enlightenment!
I declare that he is Vajrapāṇi himself;
he is indeed all the Buddhas and Tathāgatas!"
"Since there is nothing superior to the Vajrayāna.

At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, having universally observed that all Tathāgatas abide in the same single reality, stood to the right of the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, and addressed him thus:
"Blessed One!"
"What is this vajra?
At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, saying:
"You, Vajrapāṇi, are yourself the vajra."
At that time, the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, standing before the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, addressed him, saying:
"World-Honored One!
"What is this lotus?
At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Noble Avalokiteśvara, saying:
"That which is your lotus-hand is what is called 'lotus'."
At that time, all the Tathāgatas in the assembly joined their palms and addressed the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, saying:
"Regarding the lotus and the vajra you have spoken of—what is the meaning of these?"
At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, addressed all the Tathāgatas, saying:
"You should know that the four kinds of secret offerings constitute the lotus; that which abides according to the dharma upon that lotus is the vajra."

At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, wishing to reveal and explain these aforementioned phenomena that are originally devoid of intrinsic nature, again addressed the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, saying:
“World-Honored One!”
"What are the four kinds of secret offerings?
At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, saying:
"The four kinds of secret offerings are as follows:"
The Great Bodhisattva Vajralāsyā of the primary family performs the rite of great love for all Buddhas;
from her is thus born Vajramālā,
and from her is further born Vajragītā.
He further gives rise to the Vajra Dance as an offering and remains therein.
From these four secrets, all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and others are born.
Furthermore, one should visualize the seed-syllables of the great Bodhisattvas of the respective families, such as Vajralāsyā and the others.

They are as follows: *rāṃ*, *māṃ*, *yīṃ*, *nṛtya-prabhuḥ*, *hūṃ*, *aḥ*, *āttaraḥ*, *śrī-yīṃ*, *hūṃ*, *hrīḥ*, *vauṣaṭ*, *vaṣaṭ*, *phaṭ*, *maheśvara-māra*. While performing this visualization, one becomes of a single essence with them; one’s own vajra rests upon a lotus and performs the rite of magnetizing (*vaśīkaraṇa*).

When performing this rite of veneration and love, one shall attain the fruit of unsurpassed Buddha-bodhi, or become the Honored One Vajrapāṇi, or a Great Bodhisattva of the Lotus Family, or any other member of the multitude of *yuṣmanta*s.
When performing the rite of harmonious union, these bodhisattvas and others are entirely free from all stains of sin and attachment.
Thus it should be known that those great bodhisattvas of the Vajra Family enter into the Lotus Family and perform acts of veneration and love for the Tathāgata Family.

When these great bodhisattvas of the various assemblies perform this rite, they attain wondrous bliss that is neither extinguished nor exhausted; yet, within the rite they perform, there is no thought of desire.
Why is this? O Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva Mahāsattva!
Because one destroys all desires with the vajra, one thereby attains the supreme secret lotus accomplishment of all *yuṣmanta*.
Furthermore, the verse says:
"Whether in the sky or in another direction, Visualize the lotus with sublime meditative equipoise;
This unsurpassed door of lotus accomplishment Yields attainment within this very life."
At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, further proclaimed the secret offerings such as the Vajra-play.
He spoke in verse:
“O Supreme Bodhisattva among all Bodhisattvas!”
Vajralāsyā of great renown;
likewise Ratnamālā, Gītā, and Nṛtyā, who are perfectly equipoised—
these are the four secret Bodhisattvas!
This is the adamantine secret offering;
it is an offering to all Buddhas and Tathāgatas!
According to the ritual, one should constantly perform acts of veneration and endearment.
"Furthermore, one should visualize the secret seed-syllables of the Bodhisattvas according to the Dharma.
They are as follows: *tāram arāgamam nirmāṇa-duravāraṃ*. Furthermore, the verse says:"
"When visualizing, one should form the triple-pronged mudrā, with the vajra resting upon a lotus;
through the dharmas such as Vajralāsyā and others, one attains inexhaustible bliss through accomplishment."

"Furthermore, it should be known that the method of secret offering is the samādhi-gate of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara. Within this gate, the Bodhisattva Vajralāsyā is subsumed; all the Bodhisattvas Tārā and Bhṛkuṭī are of one and the same essence without distinction. The Bodhisattva Tārā, manifesting a form of love, dwells on the left side; the Bodhisattva Bhṛkuṭī, manifesting a form of love, dwells on the right side."
"These bodhisattvas, in all places, share the same single-pointed application of the supreme secret accomplishment of veneration and love.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi entered the samādhi of the Lotus-Vajra Family of all Tathāgatas. Emerging from this samādhi, he addressed the Tathāgatas with these verses:
"How marvelous is the supreme secret dharma, Which is said to abide within the lotus!
"All accomplishments are achieved in an instant, even unto the fruit of unsurpassed Bodhi.
Then, the Holy Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara spoke these verses:
"O, how great are all the Tathāgatas!"
"Pure Lotus Love is unsurpassed;
within non-self, I hold it in my hand, abiding in the lotus with the form of a lotus.
Then, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, spoke these verses for the sake of all Tathāgatas:
"Listen attentively, all Tathāgatas!
The great wisdom of the Buddhas is unsurpassed;
through its correspondence with the method of secret offerings, it brings benefit to sentient beings and accomplishes their success."
Through the practice corresponding to Vajralāsyā, my mind is firm and unshakable;
likewise, with Vajramālā and sublime song, I perform the offering of whirling dance!
All secret rites of attraction, such as this supreme and unsurpassed ritual procedure—
by practicing according to the Dharma within this secret [teaching], one immediately attains the joy bestowed by all Buddhas.
He further spoke the secret seed-syllables, namely:
"Oṃ ya ālokavajra maṇipadma. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi again addressed the Bhagavat, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, saying:
“World-Honored One!
What are the four types of secret practices: play, garlands, song, and dance?
At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, praised the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, saying:
“Excellent, excellent, Vajrapāṇi!
You have now skillfully inquired about the characteristics of secret practice; I shall now explain it to you according to the truth.”
There may be mahāsattvas who delight in the secret mode of playful sport;
there may be mahāsattvas who delight in the secret mode of precious garlands;
and there may be mahāsattvas who delight in the secret mode of sublime song.
Some mahāsattvas delight in the secret practice of circumambulatory dancing;
some mahāsattvas universally delight in the secret practices of play, garlands, song, and dance.

When one gives rise to love and joy within all such secret modes of practice, one enters, according to the inclination of the mind, the Tathāgata’s samādhi of the vajra-lotus union and attains unsurpassed secret accomplishment.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi approached the Buddha, knelt with his right knee on the ground, paid homage with his head in reverence, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

If there are true spiritual sons who are great vessels of the Dharma, they should practice and study this method of secret worship according to the principle; they will be able to accomplish all undertakings, even attaining the unsurpassed wisdom of a Buddha—how much more so for other matters that might not be accomplished?
At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, entered the empowerment of the Great Wisdom Samādhi of all Buddhas and dwelt in samādhi.

Emerging from this samādhi, he formed the secret wisdom seal (*guhyajñānamudrā*) of the Great Bodhisattva Vajralāsyā and gathered them together, causing the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi to manifest the signs of secret supernatural powers.

"It refers to the single true *dharmatā* that has been possessed from the beginning; from this, all bodhisattvas and others are born, and through the syllable 'HŪṂ' and so forth, they become great wisdom."
From this, there immediately arise the Vajra-līlā Guhyabodhisattva and all the worthy sages of the Vidyādharagarbha; all these worthy sages are identical in essence with the one true *dharmatā*.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, having received the instruction of the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, immediately spoke of the characteristics of the secret practice:
"That is to say, the ritual application according to the *vidhi* for the vast accomplishment of the Vajra-mudrā within the Tathāgata Family."

When performing recitation, one should not move the tip of the tongue; with the lips and teeth joined together and free from all vocal sounds, one should perform the recitation solely through vajra-speech. By doing so, one can accomplish all ritual procedures; this is taught as the dharma of the Bodhisattva Vajravāc.

Furthermore, regarding the ritual application within the Extensive Ritual for the Accomplishment of Secret Seals of the Vajra Family: it consists of entering the true *dharmatā* of all corresponding noble beings by means of one’s own vajra. When the secret practitioner performs this rite, they immediately attain the accomplishment of all activities; this is said to be the dharma of the Bodhisattva Vajrasattva.

Furthermore, regarding the ritual application within the *Vast Ritual Manual for the Accomplishment of Secret Seals of the Vajra Family*: it refers to those who desire to attain the ultimate, true, and eternal state of the Buddha-Bhagavān, who constantly bestow sublime bliss upon all sentient beings, and who are further able to accomplish all activities; this teaching is the Dharma of the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi again addressed all the Tathāgatas, saying:
“May the Tathāgatas listen well!

This supreme, unsurpassed secret wisdom—if one wishes to accomplish the body of all Buddhas—should dwell in tranquility with a mind in meditative equipoise (*samādhi*), entering the *samādhi* of the wisdom of all Tathāgatas. Having emerged from this *samādhi*, one attains the Buddha-body and is thereby able to accomplish the dharmas of all *samādhis*.”
Namely: the sword-accomplishing samādhi;
the yakṣiṇī-accomplishing samādhi;
The samādhi of accomplishing the *āveśa* of all seizing planets;
the samādhi of dispelling all seizing planets;
the samādhi of destroying all evils;
The samādhi of the vidyādhara;
the samādhi of the accomplishment of supernatural powers;
the samādhi of the accomplishment of wealth and jewels;
There is the samādhi for entering the palace of the asuras and achieving accomplishment;
there is the samādhi for constantly being cherished by kings and their retinues and achieving accomplishment.
Among such countless varieties of samādhi dharmas and secret chapters, these four kinds of secret offerings are the most supreme.
The Great Bodhisattva of the Vajra Family engages in play with the Bodhisattvas in accordance with the principle of *yathāvat-yoga*.

"Vajra-lāsyā" (Vajra Play) signifies the meaning of arising through union; this Bodhisattva fulfills all desires and constantly bestows joy upon all Tathāgatas. Thus, this Bodhisattva Vajra-lāsyā is the sovereign of excellence, who perpetually generates joy within all Tathāgatas.
"Furthermore, there are the secret seed-syllables, namely:

*yabū* (āḥ), *kruṣṭu*, *āḥ svāhā*, *jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ*. These syllables are the Great Bodhisattvas of the Vajra-līlā family, who are in union with the two dharmas of Vajra and Padma; it is through this very vajra that they are awakened."

All lotuses are the samādhi-gates of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara; those lotuses are free from all attachments, abide firmly through the vajra-chain, correspond with equanimity amidst all movements, and never depart from *samāhita*.

Subsequently, through the wisdom-gate of the single true syllable *HŪṂ*, one brings forth the rite of *vaśīkaraṇa* (subjugation) and is able to accomplish all activities; this teaching is the dharma of the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Noble Avalokiteśvara addressed all the Tathāgatas, saying:
"When a vajra rests upon a lotus, through the union and correspondence of these two dharmas—the vajra and the lotus—one attains sublime bliss that is neither extinguished nor exhausted."
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, standing before the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, addressed him thus:
“World-Honored One!”
How can that vajra abide upon the lotus?
Furthermore, how are the functions and characteristics of this vajra and the lotus to be explained?
“World-Honored One!
This principle is extremely profound; I am unable to understand its meaning.
At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, praised the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, saying:
“Excellent, excellent, Vajrapāṇi!

You should now know that this vajra which abides upon the lotus is for the sake of bringing benefit, happiness, and vast advantage, performing the most supreme activities of all Buddhas. Therefore, within that pure lotus, the vajra abides upon it; one enters therein and initiates the true recitation of the vajra. Subsequently, the vajra and the lotus strike against one another, accomplishing two kinds of pure milk-like appearances.”
The first is called the Vajra-milk mark; the second is called the Lotus-milk mark.
From within these two marks, there arises the auspicious and wondrous form of a great Bodhisattva;
subsequently, there further arises the fierce and wrathful form of a great Bodhisattva.

The two kinds of manifestations displayed by Bodhisattvas serve solely to discipline and benefit all sentient beings; from them arise all worthy sages, and through them all supreme undertakings are accomplished.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
What is the characteristic of milk?”
"From what, furthermore, does it arise?
We only pray that the Bhagavān will clearly reveal and explain this.
At that time, the Bhagavān addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, saying:
"That which is your own supreme secret offering, Vajrapāṇi, arises from this very 'milk-like' appearance.
The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
“I do not understand the meaning of what the Buddha has taught.
The Buddha said:
“Vajrapāṇi, you should know that the characteristic of milk is the characteristic of the fundamental reality (*dharmatā*), as described in the *Guhyatrailokyavijaya-tantra*.”

At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, universally gathered Vajrapāṇi and all other bodhisattvas, becoming of one reality, one birth, and a single body as a Vajrasattva; he then addressed the Tathāgatas, saying:

"These secret practices, such as the secret offerings now being taught, are spoken by the Buddhas and bodhisattvas in concealment solely for the purpose of awakening those among the heterodox and outsiders."

At that time, the manifested body of Vajrasattva dwells together with the bodhisattvas of his own family; through the arising of right view, he universally gathers them by means of the vajra-bind alone. All the great bodhisattvas of his own family likewise occupy their fundamental positions on the left, dwelling within lotuses. With the vajra, they awaken the lotuses, and all become associated with the same samādhi.
At that time, the assembly of great Bodhisattvas of this same family, having attained awakening, spoke these verses:
"How wonderful! O Honored One among all Perfectly Awakened Ones!
You whom I revere and love, you bestow sublime bliss;
"Only this sublime bliss exists, with nothing else beyond it; by means of it, one can accomplish the secret dharma.
At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, spoke these verses:
"How wonderful! This sublime bliss is unsurpassed; all noble beings should cultivate it."
This secret and wondrous dharma-gate should not be received by those with sinful defilements.
This unsurpassed Secret Lotus is the very dharma of Vajra-play;
the teaching of the Vajra Lotus is likewise so!
"This summarizes the wisdom of Vairocana.
When the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, spoke this verse, countless hundreds of thousands of wondrous and sublime auspicious signs appeared simultaneously.
The Sutra Spoken by the Buddha on Secret Characteristics, Volume II.
